Preserve Quality for Suitable Fresh-Fruit Products

Thematic Area: Fresh-Food Preservation & Edible Coatings

How might we preserve the quality of compatible fresh fruit for longer under the retailer’s actual storage and handling conditions?

Background

An Indonesian healthy-food retailer handles fresh produce alongside other grocery and prepared-food categories. The opportunity is to preserve saleable quality for suitable fresh-fruit products.

The objective is to assess a preservation treatment for a selected fruit against quality, selling time, application effort and cost. The application should fit the fruit’s maturity, supply route, storage conditions and handling practices.

Relevant partners offer edible coatings, post-harvest treatment, application equipment and produce-quality assessment. The collaboration focuses on compatible fruits and fruit-specific treatment arrangements.

Significance of Problem

The key challenges are:

  • Reduced saleable quality: Deterioration reduces the time fruit remains suitable for sale and affects its appearance and eating quality.
  • Lower value recovery: A shorter selling period increases markdown pressure and the risk of unsold stock.
  • Treatment economics: Application labour, material cost and additional handling determine the commercial value of a preservation treatment.

Existing Efforts

  • Available research capability: A university plant-derived edible-coating technology regulates gas exchange and provides antibacterial and antifungal protection for compatible fruits, including mangoes, avocados and papayas. The technology is at TRL6 with laboratory and field testing.
  • First application: Choose a compatible fruit and compare treated and untreated batches with similar maturity and handling. Measure quality over time, acceptable selling days, appearance, taste, application effort and net value recovered.
  • Collaboration focus: Develop the fruit-specific formulation and application workflow, arrange material supply and food-use documentation, and set quality acceptance criteria. Maintain consistent storage controls throughout the application and selling period.

Potential Market Size

  • Global produce-loss context: Fruits and vegetables experienced an estimated 25.4% loss worldwide in 2023 across stages after harvest and before retail. This highlights the scale of the global produce-preservation opportunity.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
